cells.tense: You have the pen now, and the room is exactly here.
cells.act: release what is done and keep what serves
cells.ask: Name what you still carry that's already finished — a grudge, a role, a way of being fair with someone — and set it down. Then decide what stays. No clock.
cells.core:
Being fair with people is settled in you, and it doesn't come out of arguing with yourself. Something rises in a moment and the call is already formed — soaked in feeling and steady at once. You answer from there. It isn't cold and it isn't a reckoning you talk yourself through.

What this balance can feed next is release. There's a posture of fairness you took on for a reason that's since passed, and it can be put down — not because it failed, but because it's finished. The same sense that knows what to hold also knows what's done, and both can be trusted at once. Letting the old shape go won't blunt the call. It'll show you what actually remains standing.
cells.sheetLine: The old fairness can go. Your call stays.
cells.verb: Setting a fair emotional read that governs what happens next
cells.place: Standing where what you are has no shadow left to hide in

cells.tense: You're bracing for a verdict that the present moment isn't asking you to make.
cells.act: hold the weight as a builder holds stone
cells.ask: Wherever you're settling the fairness ahead of time, carry only your own part for a week. No pre-deciding, no evening out, no ruling on what hasn't happened. Answer only what's asked, when it's asked.
cells.core:
Deciding it fair before it happens has started steering the room. The right answer is chosen ahead of time, so nothing arrives clean. Conversations carry their ruling before they start, and the people in them can feel it coming. Something is being contained that doesn't need containing yet, and the containing is the weight.

There's a way back that doesn't make you unfair. It's the strong hold, not the tight grip. Take one place where you're bracing — a talk, a call, a choice — and carry only your own part into it. Hold the stone the way a builder does: steady, ready, not pressing down. What's fair in that moment will come when the moment comes. The end doesn't have to be built before the beginning.
cells.sheetLine: The verdict is getting decided before anything happens.
cells.verb: Setting a fair emotional read that governs what happens next
cells.place: Standing where what you are has no shadow left to hide in

cells.tense: You're still standing at a door that closed a long time ago.
cells.act: write the facts down in order, without feeling words
cells.ask: Take one stuck situation and put only the sequence on paper — what happened, in order, no feeling words, no ought-to-have. One page. Read it back when it's done, and let the ruling wait.
cells.core:
The fair read isn't landing where it used to. Something in you is still back at an earlier moment, holding a shape that made sense then. Here, the signal is quiet or late. You can tell something is off, but the usual quick sense of what's fair isn't arriving on time.

Start with facts. Not the account of them — the facts themselves, plainly. One situation, the actual order of it, stripped of feeling words and blame. What came first, what came next. No ruling at the end. Put it on paper because paper doesn't need you to feel anything first. Then read it once. The clarity this rebuilds is structural, not emotional, and it's what carries the fairness back in.
cells.sheetLine: Put the sequence on paper. No feeling words.
cells.verb: Setting a fair emotional read that governs what happens next

cells.tense: The pen is down in a room you're already writing in, and you'd call that the room.
cells.act: listen as a student of it
cells.ask: Where your read is strong, hold one real question open about it — something you truly don't know — before you decide anything. No clock, no announcement. Hear what else is there.
cells.core:
The emotional territory is being steered — kept fair, decided, held — and asked about it, you'd call it what the room needed. The read is there, it's working, it's yours. It's filed under circumstance, or the shape of the group, or someone's personality. What's yours to notice isn't the fairness itself. It's that the reading is coming through you.

A smaller, older form of the same line is close at hand, and it asks for no claim of mastery. It's the listening that precedes knowing — the part with no answer yet, and no embarrassment about that. Take one situation where your read is strong and hold one real question open about it. Not a rhetorical question. Not a soft landing for the read you already have. Stay a student of it, and hear what else is there.
cells.sheetLine: The reading is coming through you. Filed under the room.
cells.verb: Setting a fair emotional read that governs what happens next
cells.place: Standing where what you are has no shadow left to hide in
